metadata.country_note: Reference evidence does not establish approval or field effectiveness at the user location.
metadata.selection_basis: Curated referenced alternatives, not comparative efficacy rankings or a tank-mix instruction. Up to two eligible references per result.
metadata.scope_note: International reference evidence with source jurisdiction retained. No default country registration is inferred.
metadata.rule_count_note: R01-R13 preserve application and mixed selection policies; R14-R17 add sourced care contexts. Rules are not independently validated efficacy claims.

policy.priority_meaning: Higher number means earlier display, not efficacy, severity or probability.

Anthracnose.summary: Reduce water splash and check lower leaves for new spots.

Bacterial.summary: The model identifies a broad bacterial pattern. Focus on hygiene and limiting splash.

medication.summary: The bacterial label is too broad to select a targeted medication.

Bottom_Rot.summary: Inspect the plant base and manage residue and drainage around affected plants.

medication.summary: These options may help prevent bottom rot. They will not restore heads that are already rotting.

Downy_Mildew.summary: Keep foliage dry where possible and inspect the undersides of leaves.

Healthy.summary: Continue routine crop care and watch for changes. No disease-specific action is selected.

medication.summary: No disease medication suggested for a healthy result.

Lettuce_Mosaic_Virus.summary: Focus on limiting spread and protecting subsequent plantings.

medication.summary: No chemical cure for infected plants. Focus on limiting spread and using healthy planting material.

Powdery_Mildew.summary: Inspect both leaf surfaces and track whether powdery growth spreads.

Septoria_Blight.summary: Reduce splash, clear old crop debris and monitor neighbouring lettuce.

Viral.summary: This broad label does not identify a particular virus. Prioritise monitoring and prevention of spread.

medication.summary: No chemical cure for infected plants. This broad viral label does not identify an insect vector.

Wilt_and_Leaf_Blight.summary: Check leaves, the plant base and water delivery together; this combined label does not establish one cause.

medication.summary: The combined wilt and leaf-blight label is too broad to select a targeted medication.

retake_image.title: Take a clearer leaf photograph
retake_image.detail: Photograph one affected leaf in daylight, with the whole leaf visible and the symptoms in focus.
retake_image.reason: The image result does not yet support disease-specific advice.

routine_monitor.title: Check nearby plants
routine_monitor.detail: Look at leaf surfaces and the plant base. Record any new spots, wilting or insects and compare photographs over time.
routine_monitor.reason: Regular observations help identify a developing problem.

steady_moisture.title: Keep root-zone moisture steady
steady_moisture.detail: Check the bed or growing medium before watering; avoid both drying out and prolonged saturation.
steady_moisture.reason: Lettuce needs consistent moisture for growth.

dry_foliage.title: Limit water splash onto leaves
dry_foliage.detail: Direct irrigation to the root zone where possible. If overhead watering is needed, use morning conditions that let leaves dry promptly.
dry_foliage.reason: Splash and persistent leaf wetness can favour several lettuce leaf diseases.

clean_tools.title: Clean crop-handling tools
clean_tools.detail: Remove plant residue from tools and clean them between affected and unaffected crop areas.
clean_tools.reason: Contaminated handling equipment can move plant material between plants.

remove_debris.title: Clear old crop debris
remove_debris.detail: Collect old leaves and crop waste around the growing area and keep them away from the current crop.
remove_debris.reason: Old plant material can carry pathogens into another crop.

healthy_seed.title: Start the next planting with healthy seed
healthy_seed.detail: Choose seed with a documented health-testing history and start with symptom-free seedlings.
healthy_seed.reason: Good planting material reduces one route by which crop problems are introduced.

anthracnose_scout.title: Inspect lower leaves and midribs
anthracnose_scout.detail: Look for new spots on lower leaves and along the underside of the midrib; record the affected area of the bed.
anthracnose_scout.reason: These are useful places to track the anthracnose pattern.

anthracnose_rotation.title: Plan a break from lettuce in affected soil
anthracnose_rotation.detail: For a future crop, choose a non-lettuce rotation or a different bed with no recorded anthracnose history.
anthracnose_rotation.reason: The pathogen can persist in soil; rotation may reduce carryover.

bacterial_residues.title: Avoid carrying diseased residue into the next crop
bacterial_residues.detail: Clear affected crop remains before replanting and avoid consecutive lettuce crops on uncleared infected soil.
bacterial_residues.reason: This is a shared residue-management practice for bacterial leaf problems, not identification of a bacterial species.

bottom_inspect.title: Inspect the base of the lettuce plant
bottom_inspect.detail: Look beneath outer leaves and around the crown for sunken, brown or decaying tissue. Photograph the base separately.
bottom_inspect.reason: A leaf-only image may miss the main area affected by bottom rot.

bottom_residue.title: Prepare a clean bed for the next crop
bottom_residue.detail: Avoid replanting into a bed with undecomposed diseased crop residues or a known recurring bottom-rot problem.
bottom_residue.reason: Residues and field disease history matter for soil-associated bottom rot.

downy_inspect.title: Inspect the underside of older leaves
downy_inspect.detail: Check beneath pale or yellow patches for light-coloured growth and record newly affected plants.
downy_inspect.reason: Downy mildew signs can be more visible on the lower leaf surface.

downy_next_crop.title: Consider disease resistance for the next planting
downy_next_crop.detail: Record the variety now grown and compare available lettuce varieties with documented downy-mildew resistance for a future planting.
downy_next_crop.reason: Resistance can help, although it varies with the pathogen population.

mosaic_vectors.title: Look for aphids on lettuce and nearby hosts
mosaic_vectors.detail: Inspect young leaves and nearby weeds for aphids and record whether colonies are increasing.
mosaic_vectors.reason: Aphids can move lettuce mosaic virus between host plants.

mosaic_reservoirs.title: Remove weed and leftover crop reservoirs
mosaic_reservoirs.detail: Manage weeds around the growing area and clear harvested lettuce remains before the next planting.
mosaic_reservoirs.reason: Weeds and leftover host plants can maintain lettuce mosaic virus.

mosaic_seed.title: Use virus-tested lettuce seed next time
mosaic_seed.detail: Keep the seed-lot record and choose lettuce seed documented as tested for lettuce mosaic virus.
mosaic_seed.reason: Infected seed is one route by which lettuce mosaic starts in a crop.

powdery_inspect.title: Track powdery growth on both leaf surfaces
powdery_inspect.detail: Inspect upper and lower surfaces and compare new photographs with today's image.
powdery_inspect.reason: Powdery and downy mildew have different signs; rainfall alone does not establish powdery mildew activity.

septoria_residues.title: Remove old lettuce leaves and manage nearby weeds
septoria_residues.detail: Clear crop remains from the production area and plan a non-lettuce break for an affected soil bed.
septoria_residues.reason: Septoria can persist through crop debris and alternate hosts.

viral_vectors.title: Check for insects without assuming one vector
viral_vectors.detail: Look for aphids, whiteflies and leafhoppers on the crop and nearby vegetation; record what is actually present.
viral_vectors.reason: Different lettuce viruses can have different insect vectors.

viral_reservoirs.title: Reduce nearby weed hosts
viral_reservoirs.detail: Keep the growing area free of weeds and record whether similar symptoms occur on neighbouring plants.
viral_reservoirs.reason: Several lettuce viruses use other plants as reservoirs; the broad model label does not identify which virus is present.

wilt_inspect.title: Check water delivery and the plant base
wilt_inspect.detail: Inspect the root zone, crown and irrigation outlets, and take a close photograph of any decay or blockage.
wilt_inspect.reason: Wilting can accompany several problems; the combined class does not identify a single pathogen.

check_drainage.title: Check drainage before adding more water
check_drainage.detail: Look for blocked drains, standing water or persistently saturated growing medium, and restore drainage where needed.
check_drainage.reason: The farmer reports a wet root zone; prolonged saturation can impair roots.

check_dry_root.title: Check water delivery to the dry root zone
check_dry_root.detail: Check emitters or the watering line and restore normal moisture gradually where water is not reaching roots.
check_dry_root.reason: The farmer reports a dry root zone.

rain_irrigation_check.title: Check the root zone before the next irrigation
rain_irrigation_check.detail: Rain is forecast or reported nearby. Check actual bed moisture before deciding the next watering amount.
rain_irrigation_check.reason: Weather is a reason to check moisture, not evidence that the bed is already wet.

protected_airflow.title: Check air movement and condensation
protected_airflow.detail: Keep air paths clear and inspect vents or circulation fans. Manage moisture while maintaining the crop's growing temperature.
protected_airflow.reason: Air movement and moisture management help reduce condensation in protected growing areas.

hydroponic_flow.title: Check solution flow and root oxygenation
hydroponic_flow.detail: Check the system's water delivery, reservoir and aeration equipment. Record root colour and any interruption to flow.
hydroponic_flow.reason: Hydroponic crop care depends on solution delivery and oxygen availability.

hydroponic_measure.title: Record solution pH, EC and temperature
hydroponic_measure.detail: Use current reservoir measurements to compare with the nutrient programme used for this system.
hydroponic_measure.reason: A soil map cannot describe the nutrient solution in a hydroponic reservoir.

soil_test_plan.title: Use the soil record for nutrient planning
soil_test_plan.detail: Keep the measured pH with the soil-test results when planning nutrients for the next application.
soil_test_plan.reason: A pH value alone does not determine a fertilizer dose or explain a leaf lesion.

downy_fosetyl_al.application_note: Primarily protects against new infection; does not restore damaged leaves.
downy_fosetyl_al.evidence_scope: Pacific Northwest lettuce guidance, March 2026; ingredient identity also in UC April 2017 guidance.

downy_mandipropamid.application_note: Protective disease management; product formulation determines application instructions.
downy_mandipropamid.evidence_scope: Pacific Northwest lettuce guidance, March 2026; ingredient identity also in UC April 2017 guidance.

powdery_quinoxyfen.application_note: The source discusses management at first symptoms; a local product schedule is not supplied.
powdery_quinoxyfen.evidence_scope: New England lettuce guidance retrieved October 2026; content revision date not stated.

powdery_azoxystrobin.application_note: Resistance-management and crop-injury restrictions depend on the product label.
powdery_azoxystrobin.evidence_scope: Pacific Northwest lettuce guidance, March 2026; ingredient identity also in UC April 2017 guidance.

anthracnose_azoxystrobin.application_note: The source links treatment timing to field history and early disease signs; no spray schedule is inferred from weather alone.
anthracnose_azoxystrobin.evidence_scope: Pacific Northwest lettuce guidance, March 2026; ingredient identity also in UC April 2017 guidance.

seedling_check.title: Inspect seedlings before they enter the crop
seedling_check.detail: Check seedling leaves and stems for spots, decay or collapse. Keep affected seedlings separate and use healthy planting material.
seedling_check.reason: Early inspection helps avoid moving visible disease into a planting.

harvest_handling.title: Prepare clean tools and gentle harvest handling
harvest_handling.detail: Clean harvest tools, avoid bruising leaves and prepare shade and prompt cooling for harvested lettuce.
harvest_handling.reason: Harvest handling affects the spread of decay and the keeping quality of lettuce.

overhead_timing.title: Time overhead watering so leaves can dry
overhead_timing.detail: Where overhead irrigation is needed, use morning conditions that allow foliage to dry. Check coverage and avoid unnecessary wetting of leaves.
overhead_timing.reason: Long periods of wet foliage and splash can support several lettuce diseases.

drip_flow_check.title: Check drip outlets for even delivery
drip_flow_check.detail: Inspect several outlets for blockage or uneven flow and check that water is reaching the root zone.
drip_flow_check.reason: Clogged drip parts can leave plants with uneven water or nutrient delivery.

bottom_azoxystrobin.application_note: The referenced use targets soil or the plant base preventively; it is not a promise to restore a rotting head.
bottom_azoxystrobin.evidence_scope: Pacific Northwest lettuce guidance, March 2026; New England ingredient confirmation.

bottom_bacillus_d747.application_note: Strain and formulation matter. This reference does not establish the performance of another Bacillus strain or a homemade culture.
bottom_bacillus_d747.evidence_scope: New England lettuce guidance retrieved October 2026; page revision date not stated.
bottom_bacillus_d747.farmer_note: Use the specified D747 strain. Do not substitute other strains or homemade cultures.

septoria_mancozeb.purpose: Fungicide option for Septoria leaf spot.
septoria_mancozeb.application_note: A protectant reference with product-specific harvest restrictions; suitability near harvest and local authorization require the actual local label.
septoria_mancozeb.evidence_scope: Australian manufacturer label APVMA 53223/139809; PDF title dated May 14, 2025.

UC_ANTHRACNOSE.title: Anthracnose: Lettuce Pest Management Guidelines
UC_ANTHRACNOSE.supports: Inspect lower leaves and midribs; reduce splashing and leaf wetness; consider a non-lettuce rotation where there is a disease history. Lists azoxystrobin for lettuce anthracnose and links timing to field history, rainfall or first symptoms.
UC_ANTHRACNOSE.limitations: California guidance. Rotation reduces inoculum but does not promise eradication. Product table is not transferred to Pakistan. California treatment table dated April 2017. It does not establish a current Pakistan lettuce label or a validated local weather trigger.

UC_BACTERIAL.title: Bacterial Leaf Spot: Lettuce Pest Management Guidelines
UC_BACTERIAL.supports: Use healthy seed, reduce sprinkler splash, and avoid carrying infected lettuce residues into consecutive crops.
UC_BACTERIAL.limitations: The dataset label Bacterial is broader than the pathogen described here. Only shared hygiene and water-management practices are applied, with no pathogen reassignment.

UC_BOTTOM_ROT.title: Rhizoctonia Diseases: Lettuce Pest Management Guidelines
UC_BOTTOM_ROT.supports: April 2017 guidance supports bed hygiene and disease-history checks. Its statement that no fungicides are effective is historical and conflicts with newer regional treatment guidance.
UC_BOTTOM_ROT.limitations: Retained for cultural care and historical transparency. Medication coverage now uses the March 2026 PNW handbook and the New England guide; efficacy varies by region, pathogen and application.

UC_DOWNY.title: Downy Mildew: Lettuce Pest Management Guidelines
UC_DOWNY.supports: Inspect lower leaf surfaces; reducing leaf wetness can help; choose resistance when planning subsequent plantings. Names fosetyl-Al and mandipropamid for lettuce downy mildew; describes mainly protective fungicide use.
UC_DOWNY.limitations: April 2017 table. Its dimethomorph supplemental-label entry expires in December 2018 and is excluded. Current ingredient references use newer guidance; foreign rates and approval are not transferred.

UC_MOSAIC.title: Lettuce Mosaic: Lettuce Pest Management Guidelines
UC_MOSAIC.supports: Virus-tested seed, weed and crop-residue management, and aphid monitoring support prevention.
UC_MOSAIC.limitations: Applied to Lettuce_Mosaic_Virus only; California seed-testing ordinances and crop calendars are not presented as Pakistan requirements.

UC_POWDERY.title: Powdery Mildew: Lettuce Pest Management Guidelines
UC_POWDERY.supports: Inspect both leaf surfaces for powdery growth; distinguish powdery from downy mildew. Powdery mildew is not treated as a rain-driven disease. Names quinoxyfen and azoxystrobin for lettuce powdery mildew, and discusses treatment at first symptoms and product-specific restrictions.
UC_POWDERY.limitations: The California chemical table is not a Pakistan lettuce product label. California treatment table dated April 2017. No foreign product, dose, PHI, resistance-group number or organic claim is transferred.

CORNELL_SEPTORIA.title: Septoria leaf spot on lettuce
CORNELL_SEPTORIA.publisher: Cornell University, Long Island Vegetable Health
CORNELL_SEPTORIA.supports: Remove crop debris, manage alternate hosts, and use crop rotation to address carryover.
CORNELL_SEPTORIA.limitations: Source text retrieved from the search index; direct fetch returned HTTP 502 on the access date. Seed and irrigation actions are independently supported by other listed sources. Direct retrieval also failed during the 2026-10-07 review; inherited details are not newly verified.

UC_VIRUSES.title: Spinach and Lettuce Virus Diseases
UC_VIRUSES.supports: Virus symptoms overlap; different viruses have different insect vectors. Healthy seed and limiting insect access support prevention; symptomatic plants have no practical virus cure.
UC_VIRUSES.limitations: The inherited Viral label does not identify a virus or its specific vector. The app does not prescribe a vector-specific insecticide.

NC_LETTUCE.title: Lettuce Production in North Carolina
NC_LETTUCE.supports: Regular scouting, consistent moisture without prolonged saturation, irrigation checks and fertilizer planning based on soil tests.
NC_LETTUCE.limitations: Regional planting calendars, cultivar recommendations, fertilizer rates and numerical soil targets are not copied into the Pakistan system.
NC_LETTUCE.document_date_basis: Page explicitly says reviewed/revised December 28, 2025; originally published January 1, 2001.

UMD_LETTUCE.title: Growing Lettuce in a Home Garden
UMD_LETTUCE.supports: Avoid excessive watering; if overhead irrigation is used, choose morning so foliage can dry during the day.
UMD_LETTUCE.limitations: Timing guidance supports a scheduling suggestion; forecast rain does not establish actual root-zone moisture.

EO_LETTUCE.title: Disease Management in Organic Lettuce Production
EO_LETTUCE.publisher: Ohio State University plant pathologists / eOrganic, hosted by Oregon State University
EO_LETTUCE.supports: Clean tools, remove old plant debris, manage weeds, use healthy seed and avoid poorly drained conditions.
EO_LETTUCE.limitations: General practices only. Organic certification, amendments, seed-treatment recipes and chemical/biological product claims are not transferred to Pakistan.

UMASS_HUMIDITY.title: Reducing Humidity in the Greenhouse
UMASS_HUMIDITY.supports: Air movement and moisture management help limit condensation; appropriate ventilation can exchange humid air while maintaining crop temperature.
UMASS_HUMIDITY.limitations: General greenhouse guidance, not a lettuce infection model. Direct retrieval returned HTTP 403 during the 2026-10-07 review; inherited details and date are not newly verified. The app's 90% RH attention trigger is a manual attention policy, not a universal biological threshold. A separately retrieved UF/IFAS source supports the general airflow practice.
UMASS_HUMIDITY.document_date_basis: No date newly verified; the inherited record carried 2026-06-16.

UF_HYDROPONIC.title: Growing Lettuce in Small Hydroponic Systems
UF_HYDROPONIC.supports: Monitor solution pH, EC, temperature and oxygenation; check irrigation flow and scout hydroponic crops. Keep procedure records.
UF_HYDROPONIC.limitations: Small-system guidance. The app does not prescribe a universal pump cycle, solution recipe or dosing rate; system-specific targets differ.

PAK_DPP.title: List of Registered Pesticides in Pakistan
PAK_DPP.supports: Official index of Pakistan pesticide registration resources.
PAK_DPP.limitations: Index availability does not demonstrate a current product label for lettuce, a target disease or a particular protected/hydroponic use. No product-specific Pakistan lettuce entry was established in this release. Search-index access succeeded; direct fetch did not. Direct retrieval also failed during the 2026-10-07 review; inherited details are not newly verified.

PAK_REVUS_SCOPE.title: Revus Start: Pakistan product uses
PAK_REVUS_SCOPE.supports: Page lists mandipropamid plus cymoxanil with potato and melon uses. Lettuce was not listed at review.
PAK_REVUS_SCOPE.limitations: Retrieved page lists potato/melon uses, not lettuce. This does not establish that no Pakistan lettuce product exists, and it does not authorize transferring overseas lettuce use.

PNW_BOTTOM_ROT.title: Lettuce (Lactuca sativa) - Bottom Rot
PNW_BOTTOM_ROT.publisher: Oregon State University, Washington State University and University of Idaho Extension
PNW_BOTTOM_ROT.supports: Lettuce bottom-rot page lists chemical and biological references; drainage and rotation remain part of management.
PNW_BOTTOM_ROT.limitations: Regional extension reference, not proof of registration at the user location or universal efficacy. No application rates or product authorizations are transferred.
PNW_BOTTOM_ROT.document_date_basis: Page explicitly states latest revision March 2026.

PNW_DOWNY.title: Lettuce (Lactuca sativa) - Downy Mildew
PNW_DOWNY.publisher: Oregon State University, Washington State University and University of Idaho Extension
PNW_DOWNY.supports: Lettuce downy-mildew page lists Aliette and Revus references and distinguishes protective management and resistance groups.
PNW_DOWNY.limitations: Regional extension reference, not proof of registration at the user location or universal efficacy. No application rates or product authorizations are transferred.
PNW_DOWNY.document_date_basis: Page explicitly states latest revision March 2026.

PNW_POWDERY.title: Lettuce (Lactuca sativa) - Powdery Mildew
PNW_POWDERY.publisher: Oregon State University, Washington State University and University of Idaho Extension
PNW_POWDERY.supports: Lettuce powdery-mildew page lists Quadris references; protective treatment and resistance management are emphasized.
PNW_POWDERY.limitations: Regional extension reference, not proof of registration at the user location or universal efficacy. No application rates or product authorizations are transferred.
PNW_POWDERY.document_date_basis: Page explicitly states latest revision March 2026.

PNW_ANTHRACNOSE.title: Lettuce (Lactuca sativa) - Anthracnose
PNW_ANTHRACNOSE.publisher: Oregon State University, Washington State University and University of Idaho Extension
PNW_ANTHRACNOSE.supports: Lettuce anthracnose page lists Quadris references alongside sanitation, rotation and weed management.
PNW_ANTHRACNOSE.limitations: Regional extension reference, not proof of registration at the user location or universal efficacy. No application rates or product authorizations are transferred.
PNW_ANTHRACNOSE.document_date_basis: Page explicitly states latest revision March 2026.

NE_LETTUCE_DISEASE.title: Lettuce, Endive and Escarole: Disease Control
NE_LETTUCE_DISEASE.publisher: New England Vegetable Management Guide / UMass Amherst
NE_LETTUCE_DISEASE.supports: Lettuce sections identify azoxystrobin and Bacillus amyloliquefaciens D747 for bottom rot, and quinoxyfen for powdery mildew.
NE_LETTUCE_DISEASE.limitations: No content revision date was visible; 2026 copyright is not a publication date. Local registration and efficacy were not established.

UMASS_SEPTORIA.title: Lettuce, Septoria Blight
UMASS_SEPTORIA.supports: Supports healthy seed, transplant inspection, reducing splash and leaf wetness, residue management and weed control.
UMASS_SEPTORIA.limitations: Historical cultural-care guidance. It refers readers elsewhere for current chemical recommendations and is not used to select a fungicide.
UMASS_SEPTORIA.document_date_basis: Page explicitly states last updated January 14, 2014.

KENDON_MANCOZEB_LABEL.title: Kendon Mancozeb WG Agricultural Fungicide: manufacturer label, APVMA 53223/139809
KENDON_MANCOZEB_LABEL.supports: Label identifies mancozeb 750 g/kg; its lettuce row includes Septoria leaf spot. Used only to support a generic active-ingredient reference.
KENDON_MANCOZEB_LABEL.limitations: PDF cover and lettuce row were visually checked. Date comes from PDF title, not a regulator approval date. Live registration status was not independently verified. Foreign formulation, rates and withholding interval are not adopted.
KENDON_MANCOZEB_LABEL.document_date_basis: PDF title specifies conversion file 14 May 2025; hosted in June 2025 directory. Legal approval date not established.

R01.name: withhold_actions
R01.description: Block advice when diagnosis is missing, failed or unrecognized.

R02.name: select_class_actions
R02.description: Use scope and explicit uncertainty to select disease or general care.

R03.name: preserve_broad_label
R03.description: Retain broad dataset categories without inferring pathogen species.

R04.name: hydroponic_context
R04.description: Use nutrient-solution care for hydroponics and exclude soil-bed actions.

R05.name: respond_to_root_observation
R05.description: Respond to reported wet or dry root-zone conditions without inferring moisture from weather.

R06.name: prioritise_airflow_check
R06.description: Select an airflow check for protected cultivation; increase its priority when a fresh humidity reading reaches the manual 90% RH attention trigger. This is not a validated infection threshold.

R07.name: avoid_outdoor_proxy
R07.description: Do not substitute outdoor humidity for measured inside humidity.

R08.name: schedule_moisture_check
R08.description: Use outdoor precipitation to prompt an actual root-zone moisture check.

R09.name: use_ph_as_background
R09.description: Use a current, vetted soil pH record as nutrient-planning background without computing a dose. Stale pH does not trigger an action.

R10.name: apply_report_feedback
R10.description: Apply one bounded reporting feedback exclusion request.

R11.name: omit_incompatible_action
R11.description: Exclude actions incompatible with the root system or growing environment.

R12.name: rank_actions
R12.description: Rank eligible actions using manual attention scores; scores are not efficacy.

R13.name: select_medication
R13.description: Select sourced international treatment references only within diagnosis and setup eligibility.

R14.name: seedling_check
R14.description: Select seedling check when the farmer supplies growth_stage=seedling. Action evidence supports the practice; the display priority is a manual application choice.

R15.name: harvest_handling
R15.description: Select harvest handling when the farmer supplies growth_stage=near_harvest. Action evidence supports the practice; the display priority is a manual application choice.

R16.name: overhead_timing
R16.description: Select overhead timing when the farmer supplies irrigation=overhead. Action evidence supports the practice; the display priority is a manual application choice.

R17.name: drip_flow_check
R17.description: Select drip flow check when the farmer supplies irrigation=drip. Action evidence supports the practice; the display priority is a manual application choice.
